title: 8th Sitting of third session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 with 28 members present. The Speaker announced a Judiciary Committee change and members held the preliminary debate on a resolution by the South Galolhu member calling on the government to disclose its agreement with UAE-based Eagle Hills on the Rasmale 'Maldives Waterfront and Marina' project, which the mover said hands over 500+ hectares for 99 years with no acquisition cost or rent. Government-aligned members called the resolution unnecessary, said the project was already transparent and would bring investment, jobs and housing, while MDP members raised secrecy, sovereignty and influence concerns; the Speaker upheld a point of order after the Kendhoo member called the President a Jew. After a 10:30-11:00 break, the Vilifushi member presented a government bill amending the Income Tax Act (Law 2019/25) to cap deductible interest at 25% of tax EBITDA from 2027, and debate on it had just begun when this part ends; some passages are jumbled in the source text. This part continues the preliminary debate on the government bill amending the Income Tax Act (Law 25/2019), which changes how much loan interest companies can deduct from taxable profit (capped at 25%), starting in 2027. Supporters said it closes loopholes used by multinationals, aligns the Maldives with international standards and could ease foreign borrowing; critics said it adds tax burden on businesses and foreign investors while extra revenue goes to recurrent spending. After the debate closed, the bill was accepted 39-8 and sent to the Committee of the Whole House. The part opens mid-speech from a member whose header is in part 1, and the chair noted the next sitting is on 26 October 2026.

items.title: Announcement of change to Judiciary Committee membership
items.outcome: announced: Kendhoo member replaces Kanditheemu member (MDP seat) from 20 Oct 2026

items.title: Resolution calling on the government to disclose all details of the agreement with Eagle Hills on the Rasmale project
items.outcome: debated (preliminary debate), no vote in this part

items.title: Bill to amend the Income Tax Act (Law 2019/25), submitted on behalf of the government
Preliminary debate on the bill to amend the Income Tax Act (Law No. 25/2019), submitted for the government by Vilufushi MP Hassan Waheed
Voting on items that reached the voting stage
items.outcome: Income Tax Act amendment bill accepted 39-8, sent to Committee of the Whole House

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the Rasmale project as a way to raise state revenue for health, welfare and housing.
Said MDP did not bring resolutions when an Addu fishing area and the international airport were handed over under its government.
Raised a point of order objecting to the Kendhoo member calling the President a Jew.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said the government promised the Fushidhiggaru/Rasmale reclamation would solve housing, and that promises have not been kept.
Called on citizens to oppose giving a large area free for 99 years, citing no acquisition cost.
Described the President as a Jew and Zionist supporter; the Speaker upheld a point of order against this.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Rejected the Kendhoo member's remarks about the President as untrue.
Said MDP sought the same rule change in the 19th Majlis to vote before debating urgent motions and resolutions.
Urged MDP members not to oppose the Eagle Hills project and suggested other matters for resolutions.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Said the MDP-majority Majlis refused funding for the reclamation the President prioritised, and the mover was among them.
Said there is no secrecy: the developer briefed media and took questions.
Said the government is building housing outside the budget.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Began by asking how the interest cap fits with recent talk of attracting foreign investors; speech continues beyond this part.
Said tax revenue rose from 22.8 billion in 2023 to about 30 billion in 2026 while recurrent spending rose similarly.
Argued the bill is stricter than international norms by disallowing carry-forward of unused deductions.
Said it will deter foreign investment and called for spending cuts instead.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Fully supported the section 71 amendments as reducing tax avoidance.
Said modernising tax law builds trust with international institutions and investors.
Began discussing the Eagle Hills resolution; the chair said that debate was not yet concluded.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Moved the resolution: the Eagle Hills commercial terms agreement is undisclosed, gives 500+ hectares for 99 years without acquisition cost or rent.
Cited constitutional articles 250, 251 and 29 on state property, territory and right to information.
Criticised a proposed rule change he said would limit members' ability to bring such resolutions.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Called the resolution unnecessary, saying the government and investor have briefed media and parties on the project.
Said the 20th Majlis required such deals to be done by law and the government will submit that law.
Supported the planned rule change limiting such resolutions.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Compared the project's USD 20 billion over 10 years with about USD 6.7 billion invested in tourism since 1972.
Said the project should be accepted if it brings benefits and prosperity to Maldivians.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said he does not oppose foreign investment but this project is of unprecedented size and type.
Raised concern that investor money and influence could reach members and governments.
Said the deal should be examined carefully before proceeding.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Said some agreement details are already in the resolution, suggesting some members have the agreement.
Said MDP members previously sold Enboodhoo lagoon.
Argued the project will create good jobs and similar projects should be done in other large lagoons.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said the previous government left large debt and called the reclaimed land empty at the time.
Said a USD 20 billion investment far exceeds past foreign investment of hundreds of millions a year.
Said opponents' claims about the project lack factual basis.

speakers.name: Hassan Waheed
positions: Presented the Income Tax Act amendment to cap interest deductions at 25% of tax EBITDA and remove exemptions in section 71.
Said it closes loopholes multinationals use to avoid tax, aligns with international standards, applying from tax year 2027.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Said the amendment closes loopholes that let large multinationals avoid tax.
Argued aligning with international standards will improve how the IMF and World Bank view the Maldives and ease loans.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Said the changes to section 71 bring the tax system in line with global practice to attract foreign investment.
Argued the 25% interest deduction cap is clearly defined and will make foreign loans easier.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Thanked the sponsor and the government for strengthening the tax system, which funds about 70% of the budget.
Said the reform targets companies that manipulate accounts to avoid tax; noted implementation starts in 2027.
Accused the MDP of spreading misleading claims about reforms.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the amendment as reducing abuse when foreign parties move money out of the country.
Said it revises rules on deducting interest when calculating taxable income, in consultation with MIRA.

decisions: Speaker announced Kendhoo member Mauroof Zakir replaces Kanditheemu member Ameen Faisal on the Judiciary Committee (MDP seat) from 20 October 2026
Speaker upheld the South Feydhoo member's point of order on the Kendhoo member calling the President a Jew
Debate time allocated at 4 hours each for the Eagle Hills resolution and the Income Tax amendment bill
Preliminary debate on the Income Tax Act (Law 25/2019) amendment bill concluded.
Income Tax Act amendment bill accepted by Parliament (39 yes, 8 no) and sent to the Committee of the Whole House under rule 106(r).
Chair announced the next sitting on Monday 26 October 2026 at 9:00.

votes.what: Acceptance of the bill to amend the Income Tax Act (Law No. 25/2019); 49 present, 47 voted, 24 needed
